newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton ends slightly up, May options expire.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton ends slightly up, May options expire.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures closed barely firmer after the U.S. Department of Agriculture issued a mostly neutral supply and demand report, market sources said.

The USDA raised world ending stocks by five percent to 37.8 million bales, due mainly to an increase in China's output. The State Statistical Bureau put China's crop at 19.3 million bales in its most recent estimate.
The USDA also increased its forecast for U.S. exports to 7.0 million bales from 6.8 million bales, and cut U.S. ending stocks to 3.95 million bales from 4.15 million bales.
Players had largely anticipated the revision, analysts said, attributing today's range from 71.85 to 71.20 basis May, to the options expiry.
"This morning's report is not enough to either exacerbate bearishness or lift us out of the doldrums," Sharon Johnson, an analyst with Frank Schneider and Co Inc, said.
She estimated that the speculators are between 22 percent to 24 percent net short, adding that the front month may have run out of downward momentum.
The spot month ended 0.33 cent higher at 71.69 cents per lb, while the back months settled unchanged to 0.34 higher.
Volume was estimated at 11,500 lots compared with Thursday's official 11,381 lots.
Open interest fell 868 lots to 29,582 lots, as of Wednesday's close. The first notice day for May cotton is April 24.
